title: Correct briefly, retest later
statement: Correct an error immediately and briefly, test it, give other items, then retest it later.
example: One lesson-authoring skill keeps corrective feedback to 40 words or fewer, with the passage in view, followed by a correct-test-retest flow.
detail: Among the direct-instruction and practice rules a course review applied as its standard: error correction should be immediate and brief (correct, test, give intervening items, then retest later), and too much feedback can reduce active processing, so feedback timing should shift as proficiency improves (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0086-round2-feedback-brainlifts-2026-07-09.qmd`). The reading project's unpromoted lesson-authoring skill writes corrective feedback of at most 40 words with the passage visible, and follows a miss with the correct-test-retest flow (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0123-teacher-g3-reading-candidate-skill.qmd`).
against: Help before an attempt is a different matter: a later course review held that an immediately available hint lowers desirable difficulty, and the rule there is attempt first, then targeted help (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0172-g3-reading-course-feedback-2026-08-04.qmd`).

evidence.quote: - Error correction should be immediate and brief: correct, test, give intervening items, then retest later.
- Too much feedback can reduce active processing; feedback timing should shift as proficiency improves.
